html:
SMTO-SKL-0023 — This calendar invitation has too many guests

GUID: e3ac9484-d250-57be-95ac-e44e1c80e4b5
Slug: google-calendar-attendee-limit-exceeded
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • SMTO can add at most 100 guests to one calendar event, and this request had more. No invitations were sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reduce the guest list to 100 people or fewer and ask SMTO again. 100 guests is the most SMTO can add to one event.
  2. If you need to invite a larger group, invite one shared group email address that includes everyone, if your organization has one. A group address counts as a single guest but still reaches all its members.
  3. Before you confirm the new invitation, check the guest list and make sure each person should be invited. Google may email the invitation to every guest as soon as the event is saved.

What success looks like

  • The event appears in Google Calendar with the guests you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't split one meeting into several copies to fit more guests; people would get duplicate invitations.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Calendar schema validation rejected the attendees list because it exceeds the supported maximum of 100 entries.

What this means

  • Schema rejection identifies an attendee list longer than the supported maximum of 100. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Schema rejection identifies an attendee list longer than the supported maximum of 100.

How to diagnose it

  • Count explicit attendees and verify the intended recipients before reducing the list.

How to fix it

  • Supply at most 100 explicit attendee email addresses (MAX_ATTENDEES in google_calendar/models.py). Review the intended recipients before sending invitations; consider a group address for larger audiences.
  • Supply at most 100 explicit attendee email addresses. Review the intended recipients before sending invitations.

Retry and execution caution

  • Supply at most 100 explicit attendee email addresses. Review the intended recipients before sending invitations.

How to verify the fix

  • The deliberate attendee list contains at most 100 supported addresses.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
